status_summary: On 2025-03-31 the Eastern District of Texas, in consolidated suits by laboratory groups (American Clinical Laboratory Association v. FDA), vacated FDA's May 2024 laboratory-developed test rule in full, holding that FDA lacks authority to regulate laboratory-developed test services, and remanded to HHS. On 2025-09-19 FDA published a final rule, effective that day, that describes the decision as a final judgment and removes the 2024 wording on laboratory manufacturers from 21 CFR 809.3(a), restoring the earlier text. This settles the FDA side of the overlapping authority question for now but does not create the test-sharing mechanism or the revised rules for modified tests that the document recommends.

timeline.event: Eastern District of Texas vacates and sets aside FDA's laboratory-developed test final rule in full in American Clinical Laboratory Association v. FDA and a consolidated case, holding FDA lacks authority over laboratory-developed test services, and remands to HHS.
FDA publishes a final rule implementing the vacatur by removing the 2024 phrase on laboratory manufacturers from 21 CFR 809.3(a), effective on publication.
